body.statement: Suppose \(C>0\) and the sequential multiscale certificate holds without a dyadic loss, with \(T_\beta\) large enough that \(L_T\le T/4\). Then, for every \(T\ge T_\beta\), \[\frac{\kappa_\beta}{2}\min\{B^2,(B\wedge C)^2\}T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}\le R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)\le K_+(B,C,\beta)T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}.\] Thus \(R_T^{(2)}(\beta;B,C)=\Theta_{B,C,\beta}(T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)})\) over all sequential policies and all estimators.
body.justification: This downstream theorem assembles the inherited upper audit and the novel certificate into the exact price of polynomial memory over the strongest sequential design comparison class.
body.gap: The matched frontier is the direct payoff from the certificate rather than a second root contribution. Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao treat finite-order regular designs, while Hu and Wager and Jia, Kallus, and Yu impose geometric stochastic mixing.
body.consumer: The result certifies that the power-law operational window is information-theoretically necessary, rather than an artifact of one estimator.
